subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should macOS Dashboard browser auth be shared-token/password-only, or may it reuse native/operator device tokens for parity with native websocket clients?
rationale: The linked issue and docs support shared-secret browser auth, but an open sibling PR intentionally preserves native-token parity; landing either behavior changes credential boundaries and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Shared-token-only browser boundary
options.body: Proceed with this direction, require the branch to cover current main's endpoint reload path, and document/prove the fallback removal before merge.

options.title: Native-token parity
options.body: Close or pause this PR and continue with the sibling parity PR after explicit security review of browser device-token injection.

options.title: Defer pending auth design
options.body: Keep both drafts open but block merge until a maintainer writes the Dashboard credential policy and expected upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Shared-token-only browser boundary
recommendation.body: Proceed with this direction, require the branch to cover current main's endpoint reload path, and document/prove the fallback removal before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the native Dashboard and authored the current-main endpoint reload path now intersecting this auth decision.
